title: Highest temperature in London on August 17?
description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 17 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent Met Office guidance points to a daytime maximum of 27°C in London on August 17 under mostly cloudy skies with light winds and only a low (10–20%) chance of showers, following the mid-August heatwave peak of 38.1°C at Kew Gardens on the 13th.** 

The breakdown of high pressure and incoming Atlantic fronts are moderating temperatures from recent highs, limiting solar heating and keeping the peak in the mid-20s. Ensemble model consensus and hourly profiles showing afternoon readings around 25–27°C underpin the market’s heavy weighting toward 26°C (51%) and 25°C (23.5%), with 27°C at 16.5%. Traders appear to price in slight downward revisions from official guidance due to greater cloud cover or minor timing shifts in frontal passage. Updated model runs and Met Office briefings on the 17th remain the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models indicate a daily maximum of 29–31°C for São Paulo on August 17, 2026, well above the August climatological average of 23–25°C.** This positions 30°C as the leading market outcome at 38.5% implied probability, followed by 29°C (27.5%) and 31°C (17.0%), with probabilities dropping sharply outside this narrow band.

The primary driver is a transient warm-air advection pattern under high pressure, delivering clearer skies, reduced cloud cover, and light northerly winds that limit cooler southerly influences typical of winter in the subtropics. Official extended forecasts from sources such as timeanddate.com (86°F/30°C), BBC Weather (30°C), and Met Office guidance (28°C) converge on this range, supported by recent model runs showing daytime peaks near 29.7°C. 

Preceding days were cooler (22°C observed on August 15), highlighting short-term variability from passing systems, but the current setup favors rapid daytime warming. Resolution will depend on the official INMET or airport station maximum; traders are pricing in modest upside risk above 31°C (5%) while assigning negligible odds to cooler outcomes, consistent with the tight clustering of forecast guidance.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent high pressure and clear skies under subtropical ridging are keeping Houston in a hot, stable pattern, with National Weather Service guidance and model consensus pointing to a daily high of 95–97°F on August 17.** 

This aligns with the market's leading 96–97°F outcome at 60% implied probability. Afternoon sea breezes and typical Gulf moisture moderate temperatures near the coast, preventing widespread 100°F readings despite strong insolation and low rain chances. Recent model runs show minimal day-to-day variability, with highs holding in the mid- to upper 90s through the weekend before a slight uptick possible Monday. Historical August averages near 95–96°F provide additional context, while the absence of tropical moisture or frontal systems reinforces trader confidence in the narrow 96–97°F bin. Updated NWS and private forecasts released in the past 24–48 hours have shown little shift, anchoring sentiment ahead of tomorrow’s observation.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 17 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/zhengzhou/ZHCC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.
